note:
ollama answers a NON-STREAMING /api/chat with a frame from the STREAMING grammar while a model loads: HTTP 200, 96 bytes, empty role, empty content, done:false, no counters. It walked three of host.py's checks unharmed — 200 is not >=400, there is no 'error' key, and `message` IS a dict whose `content` IS a str because "" is one — and died at metered_cost complaining about token counters. LOUD AT THE WRONG ORGAN (Law 7), and it cost one voyage a false sentence in an append-only history. _post now refuses it by name: HostNonFinal.

THE PREDICATE IS `"done" in body and body["done"] is not True` — PRESENT AND NOT TRUE, and the second half is the whole design. Real /api/embed responses carry NO `done` key at all, so the obvious `body.get("done") is not True` would refuse every embedding this system takes. The tooth that stands between the two forms was written FIRST, was green on HEAD, and its entire value is that it stayed green after. Order was evidence-before-assertion and deliberately inverted cheap-first: HEAD already raised on the frame, so a tooth asserting merely 'some error' would be green on a codebase with no fix in it. The discriminating tooth asserts the TYPE, and it was measured RED on HEAD through the _refuses helper's WRONG-TYPE branch — naming HostUnmetered where HostNonFinal was expected — never 'NO REFUSAL AT ALL'.

LIVE FIRE, BOTH HALVES, THROUGH THE REAL RESOLVER. Cold hex (unload, /api/ps to [], num_ctx 81920): 4 asks, 4 HostNonFinal carrying the frame verbatim, zero HostUnmetered. Warm: same ask, same num_ctx, 8 answers at cost 17, zero refusals. Plus 9 asks at default options, all answered — the guard has never bitten a good answer.

AND IT FALSIFIED A CLAIM THIS VOYAGE HAD ALREADY RECORDED. 'num_ctx is NOT the discriminator' was measured WARM, which is the wrong condition; the frame needs COLD LOAD *AND* a large num_ctx. Cold with the resolver's default options answers in ~2s and does not reproduce it. Same family as the earlier timeout story this ticket was born from: a measurement taken in the wrong condition standing in for the one that matters. The correction rides here rather than in a paragraph nobody reads.

THE WATCH IS ARMED AND ITS SPEC WAS FOUND UNBUILDABLE AS WRITTEN — the finding worth carrying forward. The ticket's `enough` counts refusals from the domain's own ask log; domain.resolve writes the inference_calls row only AFTER resolver(request) RETURNS, so a raise leaves NO ROW and refusals are invisible there. Clause one (the refusal has fired on live traffic) was satisfied AT BIRTH by the live fire, n=4, and is recorded in the verdict rather than re-measured by a probe that would have to dial the host on a clock. The probe watches the fault RETURNING instead: a post-era chat row in inference_calls with no text AND zero cost is a non-final frame that got past _post and was CACHED — worse than the misdiagnosis this ticket started from, because it stops being an error at all and is served to every future asker of that canonical question until its horizon expires. One is the finding; the clear needs 20 clean post-era chat rows. Logging refusals in domain.py is OUTSIDE constrain's `in` list and is a ticket owed, not a silent widening.
